properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at Gullwick Docks
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her; never looks anyone in the eye, keeps her gaze on the tide line; mends a net and shrugs the party off.
properties.wants: Only rows by day, never at night.
properties.knows: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; the only boat that goes near the bell water is hers.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced; 'Sella' is a dockhand spelling, the GM keeps Sela.

sources.quote: She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Where the table last saw her.

properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. Morning fog sits on the docks, gulls everywhere; pier four is where a woman mends a net on an upturned skiff.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: GM's description of the docks by day.

change.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Saltmere Mine flooded forty years ago, the same night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Links the mine's closure to the bell's origin (Sela's account, passed down from her grandmother).

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

changes.why: The fact is about the mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. An hour's walk up the cliff path. Entrance is a black mouth in the chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and a rusted cart on its side; warm air smelling of church and old candle wax. About thirty paces in the tunnel floods with warm black water; wet hymn-book pages float on it and stick to the walls.
properties.state: Closed; the tunnel is flooded with warm black water and bad air.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

changes.why: GM's own description of the mine and its current condition.

properties.what_changed: A hymn-book page from Saltmere Mine has "M. Brand" pencilled in the margin; Teo says it is Mira's handwriting and that she was there.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: The GM showed the name; the handwriting claim is Teo's, so it stays on his goal.

change.name: Is Maren Vosk in the cult?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect the harbor-master is behind the bell and the choir; nothing at the table confirms it.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: A player theory, kept as a thread only; the GM answered only 'You can think that.'

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one.

changes.why: The theory is about Maren.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof sticks out of the bay: just the bell tower and two broken arches, seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight the bell rings under the water and pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor, like a congregation, until the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation.

changes.why: GM's description of the chapel and what the party saw.

properties.statement: Fishermen say a Kelp Mother pulls children who stand near the water down by the ankles.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

changes.why: Local rumor, not a confirmed creature, so it is a rumor fact rather than an NPC.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close.

changes.why: The warning is about the water at the chapel.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: The bell rang again, louder, and the GM states the clock is at 3 of 6.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks; a fire going, smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: New place where the party stays.

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks; generous and teasing with the party.
properties.knows: Has known Maren Vosk for thirty years; says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: He runs the inn.

change.name: Maren lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay, and Bram has known her thirty years.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Bram's account of Maren's past.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: The fact is about Maren.

properties.what_is_open: Teo thinks the hymns came from the chapel, where Mira may have gone.
properties.next_step: Sela rows them out at first light and they dive to the chapel at low tide; Vessa buys rope and a second lantern tonight.
properties.deadline: First light tomorrow; Sela only rows by day.

sources.quote: Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.

changes.why: The party's plan for next session, kept as a thread since it is a player plan.

sources.quote: Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide.

changes.why: The plan depends on Sela's boat.

sources.quote: We go down to the chapel.

changes.why: The plan targets the chapel.
